because she likes him. KRYteria does not answer that question. It asks it.

Will's connections; Christine confirmed 2026-11-13 that this was a typo.

bio: Intelligent, organized, pragmatic, occasionally intimidating. Reserved until she trusts someone, then warm and funny. Financially independent, wants marriage and children, and increasingly conscious of the time involved in both. Ended an engagement some years ago and has been more deliberate since — sometimes to the point of guarding against wasted time more carefully than the situation needs.

entries.body:
Greg took me to a burger place he had clearly researched, which was sweet, and then proceeded to create what I can only describe as a greasy burger finger situation. It was all over. There was a moment where he tried to gesture with one hand while holding the burger in the other and I genuinely had to look away. I have not recovered. I laughed until I could not breathe. He was not embarrassed, he just leaned into it.

I do not know what to do with the fact that I had a better time than I have had on any date in two years.

observations.text: He chose a restaurant he had researched in advance.
A messy incident with the food, which he did not become embarrassed about.
She enjoyed the evening more than any date in two years.

evidence.rationale: Not the mess itself — that he was comfortable enough not to be humiliated by it.
He looked the place up beforehand.

entries._comment: The greasy burger finger situation maps to NOTHING about financial independence, adult competence or long-term readiness, and must not be force-mapped there just because it is the funniest thing in the file. Two evidence links, both about what it actually shows.

entries.body:
Greg mentioned he is still at his parents' place. A year out from the layoff. He said it quickly and changed the subject, which told me more than the fact did.

I keep going back and forth. He is not lazy — he plans things, he shows up, he remembers everything I say. But a year is a long time and I am 36 and I do not have a decade to find out whether someone is going to sort himself out.

observations.text: He has lived with his parents for about a year since the layoff.
He changed the subject quickly after saying it.
She read the subject change as significant.
What he has been doing about work over that year.

evidence.rationale: Living with parents after a layoff is a circumstance. It is consistent with competence and with its absence, and this entry does not separate them.

entries.body:
Asked Greg where things are with the job search. He said he has been applying, that the market is brutal for his level, and that he will have something sorted soon and then we can talk about what we are doing.

That is the third time he has said some version of 'once I have a job'. I do not think he is lying to me. I think he means it every time he says it. But I have now been told twice that the conversation happens later, and I am not sure what the trigger actually is — a job offer? any job? a certain salary? He has not said, and I have not asked, which is probably on me.

I like him so much. That is the problem. I am aware I am being more patient with this than I would be with someone I liked less and I cannot tell whether that is me being fair or me making an exception.

entries.body:
Fourth date with Jack and I have to be honest with myself. He is kind, he is stable, he has a real job, he wants children, he is on time, he is thoughtful. On paper he is the entire list.

And I do not want to kiss him. I have been waiting for that to change for a month and it has not.

It would be easier if there were something wrong with him.

observations.text: Four dates over roughly a month.
No physical attraction, unchanged over that period.
She notes he meets her stated written criteria.
